work: Church Fathers in the Patrista corpus (ANF/NPNF translations)
label: Two goats of the Atonement
def: On the Day of Atonement two like goats were taken: one was slain as a sin offering, the other, laden with the people's sins, was driven out into the wilderness.
christ: Christ in both goats: the one driven out, cursed, spat on and bound with scarlet is His passion outside the city, the other His coming again, so that they are "declarative of the two appearances of Christ" (Justin, *Dial.* 40; so also Tertullian, *Adv. Marc.* 3.7). Theodoret reads them instead as His two natures, the manhood slain and the Godhead let go.
where: Barnabas, *Ep.* 7 — “why [do you behold] the one that is accursed crowned? Because they shall see Him then in that day having a scarlet robe about his body down to his feet”
Justin, *Dial.* 40 — “of which one was sent away as the scape [goat], and the other sacrificed, were similarly declarative of the two appearances of Christ”

Tertullian, *Adv. Marc.* 3.7 — “One of these goats was bound with scarlet, and driven by the people out of the camp into the wilderness … being thus marked with all the signs of the Lord's own passion; while the other … afforded proofs of His second appearance”

Tertullian, *Adv. Jud.* 14 — “marked with manifest tokens of Christ's passion; who, after being begirt with scarlet garment, and subjected to universal spitting, and afflicted with all contumelies, was crucified outside the city”
Theodoret, *Eranistes* III — “In these two goats there is an anticipative image of the two natures of the Saviour”
